dct_description_sm: In our history two great staple trades have dominated the North, the fur trade and now, increasingly, petroleum (oil and gas). Given that Canada's North covers a vast area and has a large First Nation population, First Nation peoples and First Nation lands have played and continue to play an important part in Canadian economic development. However, unprecedented changes are occurring, including the negotiation of land claim settlements, the development of non-renewable resources, community empowerment and capacity-building. In this dynamic environment, the question that arises is how are northern indigenous groups being affected? Are land claims settlements and resource development projects providing First Nation groups the tools and/or opportunities required to meet their goals of political, social and economic well-being? Moreover, is the human security of northern indigenous groups being supported by these interacting political and economic processes?
